title: 28.2.2 Some Swarm services are not discoverable over DNS
body: After upgrading our two Docker Swarm environments, external requests to containers return 504 Gateway Timeout instead of 200. Docker Engine 28.1.1 works, while 28.2.0 and later are affected; I also tried 28.2.1 without success, and the failing environment is on 28.2.2. I see many differences between the working and failing iptables rules. Our standalone Docker environments work on 28.2.2, so this appears specific to Swarm.

symptoms_visible: After upgrading our Swarm environments to Docker 28.2.2, requests to container-backed URLs return 504 Gateway Timeout instead of 200.
The same Swarm setup works on 28.1.1, and our standalone Docker environments work on 28.2.2.
N0.label: N0 Swarm gateway timeouts reported

symptoms_visible: Requests from the Docker host or a remote host time out through Traefik, while curling localhost inside the application container succeeds and its health check remains healthy.
N1.label: N1 failure localized between Traefik and healthy tasks

symptoms_visible: Traefik still returns gateway timeouts when it tries to reach some services through the Docker overlay network.
The working and failing virtual machines otherwise use the same Debian 12 setup, kernel, and Puppet management.
N2.label: N2 Docker overlay topology established

symptoms_visible: Some tasks remain reachable while others time out, especially after tasks are redeployed or moved between nodes.
A task can reach another task on the same node while cross-node ping, curl, or TCP traffic is dropped.
Recreating the overlay network restored most services only temporarily; affected deployments worked normally again after downgrading to 28.1.1.
N3.label: N3 intermittent cross-node overlay failure characterized

symptoms_visible: A different affected operator reports that the release-candidate build restores service in their testing environment.
N4.label: N4 release candidate verified by another operator

symptoms_visible: A different affected operator reports normal service communication with the release candidate, but I have not reported a retest of that build on my original Swarm environments.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix available but original reporter not verified

question_patterns: Where are you running curl from, and can the application be reached from inside its own container?
Does the request fail from the Docker host, a remote host, or both, and are the container health checks passing?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The requests fail both from the Docker host and from a remote host. Inside the application container, curl to localhost:8080 works, so the health check passes and the container is marked healthy.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The localhost request fails inside the container too, and the container is unhealthy.
Only requests from remote hosts fail; requests made directly from every Docker host work.

question_patterns: How is the public URL routed to the service?
Is this a directly published service port or a request passing through a reverse proxy and shared network?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Traefik 3.4.1 sits in front of the containers and routes the requests. The Traefik service and application services join a shared network named proxy.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There is no reverse proxy or shared container network; the application port is bound directly on the host and fails locally.

edges.comment: Reporter c3-c4: the original reporter localized the failure to requests entering through Traefik while localhost health checks remained successful, and supplied an example application stack.

question_patterns: How was the proxy network created, and which network driver and subnet does it use?
Can you share the network definition for the proxy network?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The proxy network is created in the Traefik stack with driver: overlay. Its IPAM configuration uses subnet 192.168.220.0/22, and the application stacks refer to that already-created network as external.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The proxy network is a third-party network plugin and is not a Docker overlay network.
It is still a Docker overlay network, but it uses a different private subnet.

question_patterns: Do you have any custom network configuration in daemon.json?
Can you share the daemon network address settings?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My daemon.json sets bip to 192.168.224.1/24 and a default address pool based at 192.168.216.0/22 with size 26.

question_patterns: Besides the Docker versions, what differs between the working and failing hosts?
Are the operating system, kernel, and host configuration management the same?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Apart from the Docker versions, the VMs are identical: the same Debian 12 and kernel version, and both environments are managed the same way by Puppet.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failing hosts use a different distribution, kernel, firewall policy, and network manager from the working hosts.

question_patterns: Can you share the iptables-save headers and relevant rules from both environments?
Which iptables backend is shown by iptables-save on each host?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The failing environment's iptables-save output says v1.8.9 (nf_tables), while the working environment's output says v1.8.9 without the nf_tables marker. I also pasted the rules from both environments.

edges.comment: Reporter c8, c11, c26: the original reporter supplied daemon networking settings and confirmed that proxy is a Docker-managed overlay network. Participant3 read the backend distinction from the reporter's raw iptables-save headers; it remains contextual evidence, not the accepted root cause.

question_patterns: Does connectivity fail immediately, only after some time, or following changes such as task restarts and moves?
What cluster or service state changes occur before a service becomes unreachable?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It can work for a while and then fail. We have seen tasks become unreachable after a container is redeployed, restarted, or moved to another node, although not every moved task fails.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every service is unreachable immediately after swarm initialization, before any task restart or movement.
The delay varies between environments, but failures still appear around task redeployment or movement.

question_patterns: When a task is affected, can it communicate with services on the same node and on other nodes?
Is the failure tied to a particular node or to cross-node overlay traffic?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: A task that could not reach RabbitMQ over the overlay network worked when I constrained it onto the same worker as RabbitMQ. The failures are not tied to one particular node, and some cross-node connections are dropped while others work.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Same-node communication fails exactly like cross-node communication, including direct localhost access inside the target container.

question_patterns: Does recreating the overlay network restore communication permanently?
What happens after removing and recreating the shared network?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Recreating the Traefik overlay network and reattaching the services made nearly all services work again, but communication later broke again after more containers moved or restarted.

question_patterns: What happens if the affected Swarm nodes are returned to the previous Docker version?
Does downgrading change the connectivity behavior?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Across our affected Swarm deployments, downgrading from 28.2.2 to 28.1.1 restored service and the gateway timeout and cross-node connectivity problems went away.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failures continue unchanged after every node is downgraded to 28.1.1.
Downgrading restores connectivity, but only after the nodes are restarted.

edges.comment: Comments c12-c21 and c27-c29 merge corroborating observations from several affected Swarm operators into the simulated user side. Their deployments independently showed intermittent failures after task movement, same-node success versus cross-node loss, temporary recovery after network recreation, and recovery after downgrading. The maintainer's c17 conclusion shifted focus away from NetworkManager and iptables backend differences; c31 relayed the plan to revert the 28.2 overlay changes.

question_patterns: Could you install the release-candidate packages from the test channel in a test environment and report whether the same Swarm communication failure remains?
Please test the candidate packages against the affected workload and tell us what you observe.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We deployed v28.3.0-rc.1 in our testing environment and confirmed that it solves the problem for us. We are keeping production on the previous version until the official release passes our tests.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The release candidate still produces the same gateway timeouts and cross-node connection failures.
The release candidate restores connectivity in the test environment, but we have not yet run a long-duration production load test.

edges.comment: Participant1 c32 requested testing of the available release candidate; participant10 c33, a different affected operator, confirmed it solved the problem in their test environment. This is pre-release candidate-build verification, not confirmation from the original reporter.

solution.intent: Treat the failures as a Docker Swarm overlay-network regression introduced by the 28.2.x overlay fixes and refactoring: use 28.1.1 as the temporary rollback, then upgrade to a 28.3 build containing the reversion and verify the original Swarm workload before declaring it resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Keep affected production nodes on 28.1.1 as a temporary mitigation, then test and deploy v28.3.0 or a later build containing the reversion of the 28.2.x overlay-network changes. Verify Traefik-to-task traffic and direct cross-node TCP connectivity after task restarts or moves.
solution.inference_hint: The maintainers did not narrow the regression to a more precise internal mechanism. The accepted diagnosis is therefore limited to the 28.2.x Swarm overlay fixes/refactoring, based on the version boundary, cross-node overlay behavior, successful downgrade, planned reversion, and successful candidate-build test. Do not elevate iptables-nft, NetworkManager, DNS alone, or the later IP-exhaustion report into the final root cause.

edges.comment: Resolution chain from c17 and c31-c34: maintainers attributed the behavior to the 28.2 overlay changes, reverted that group of changes for 28.3, and a different affected operator confirmed v28.3.0-rc.1 solved their test deployment. The original reporter did not post a retest, so the terminal state records fix availability and third-party verification without claiming reporter-perceived resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause at the precision established by the thread: a regression in Docker 28.2.x Swarm overlay-network fixes/refactoring, affecting cross-node service communication after task changes; no narrower mechanism was established.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: healthy localhost requests, Traefik timeouts over a Docker overlay, intermittent cross-node failures, recovery on 28.1.1, and successful testing of the 28.3.0 release candidate by another affected operator.
Must recommend using 28.1.1 only as a temporary rollback and moving to a 28.3 or later build containing the overlay-change reversion.
Must not present recreating the overlay network as a durable fix because it restored connectivity only temporarily.
Must not settle on iptables legacy versus nft, NetworkManager, DNS alone, or the later IP-exhaustion report as the proven root cause.

Must ask the original reporter to retest a build containing the reversion, including after task restarts or moves, and must not treat another operator's release-candidate result as the original reporter's confirmation.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced production infrastructure operator who manages multiple Docker Swarm environments, Traefik stacks, custom overlay subnets, daemon configuration, and iptables output, but relies on maintainers to diagnose Docker internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and practical; provides configuration excerpts and production-versus-staging comparisons, answers follow-up questions directly, and is willing to test while protecting private service URLs.
